title: Add a regime-adaptive strategy layer: momentum → defensive factor rotation
description: The firm runs a pure momentum strategy in all market conditions. CRO is currently CRITICAL and the canary fired ORANGE 2× today. In CRITICAL/HIGH regimes, momentum names are systematically the hardest hit — we're fighting the market instead of adapting to it. A regime layer would detect the risk environment from canary + CRO signals and auto-rotate the research mandate: in GREEN regimes, pursue momentum; in ORANGE/CRITICAL, mandate defensive picks (low-beta, dividend yield, quality factor) and reduce position sizing. This doesn't require a new strategy — it's a wrapper around the existing one.
proposed_fix: Add `regime` field to canary_state.json (BULL/NEUTRAL/DEFENSIVE/CRISIS). R&D leader reads regime at assignment time and shifts sector scoring weights: in DEFENSIVE mode, boost low-volatility and dividend sectors; in CRISIS, assign only capital-preservation mandates. Manager Agent adjusts MAX_POSITION_SIZE_PCT down 30% in DEFENSIVE mode.

title: Replace flat position sizing with conviction-weighted Kelly-derived sizing
description: All approved picks receive the same capital allocation regardless of conviction score (3★ vs 5★ get identical sizing). This treats a high-conviction thesis identically to a marginal one, compressing returns. A Kelly-fraction approach — sizing proportional to edge estimate derived from conviction score, historical approval rate per agent, and sector momentum score — would concentrate capital in the firm's best ideas and reduce it in weaker ones. Even a half-Kelly implementation would improve capital efficiency.
proposed_fix: In manager_agent.py: at BUY execution, compute `size_multiplier = 0.5 + (conviction - 3) * 0.25` for conviction 3–5. Multiply MAX_POSITION_SIZE_PCT by this factor (floor 0.5×, ceiling 1.5×). Log `conviction_size_multiplier` in buy_log for post-trade attribution.
